strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout via cartTotal(items, { coupon }) in src/cart.js: 10% bulk discount at 10+ items, SAVE5 coupon applied after the bulk discount and floored at $0, unknown coupons refused, free shipping from $50 of discounted goods otherwise $4.99, empty cart costs $0. Unit tests in Vitest prove each rule and its boundaries through the public cartTotal function. Reading the code, the bulk discount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD` (strictly more than 10) while the ticket and the constant's own doc comment say "at least" 10, so the 10-item boundary case is expected to expose a defect.
inScope: cartTotal pricing: bulk discount, SAVE5 coupon, unknown coupon refusal, shipping threshold, empty cart
Boundaries: 9 vs 10 items, $50.00 vs $49.99 goods, coupon larger than goods
outOfScope: Any UI or API for checkout (none exists in the repo)
assumptions: cartTotal(items, { coupon }) in src/cart.js is the checkout pricing entry point; items are { price, quantity }.
Totals are compared as numbers rounded to cents, as cartTotal returns them.
Coupon codes are matched exactly (case-sensitive); only 'SAVE5' is tested as valid.
openQuestions: Should coupon codes be case-insensitive (e.g. 'save5')? The code treats them case-sensitively; not tested either way.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the bulk threshold: code applies the discount only above 10 items, ticket says 10 or more.
risks.mitigation: TC1 checks exactly 10 items across lines; kept as expected-to-fail with a recorded defect if the code is unchanged.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount would change totals.
risks.mitigation: TC3 uses numbers where the two orders give different totals.

risks.description: Shipping threshold computed on pre-discount subtotal or with > instead of >=.
risks.mitigation: TC6/TC7 test exactly $50.00 after a discount and $49.99.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets no bulk discount.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, and the goods never cost less than $0.
Any coupon code other than SAVE5 is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Bulk discount not applied at exactly 10 items
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items should get 10% off. src/cart.js bulkDiscount uses `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a 10-item cart gets no discount (contradicting the ticket and the constant's own "at least" doc comment). Should be `>=`.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:3,quantity:4},{price:3,quantity:6}]) returns 34.99 instead of 31.99; TC1 passes only as it.fails.

review.standard: Known-defect tests must fail for the documented reason only (an assertion that can pass for the wrong reason)
review.summary: TC1's it.fails passes on any failure inside the test, not only the documented `> BULK_THRESHOLD` defect, so it doesn't prove the defect is the cause.
review.failureScenario: With the current code, cartTotal on 10 x $3 returns 34.99 (no discount), the toBe(31.99) assertion fails and it.fails reports green, which is correct. But if cartTotal threw a TypeError, or a later regression made it return a different wrong value such as 30 after the threshold is fixed, it.fails would still report green and hide it. Suggested fix: add a comment or a sibling assertion pinning the current defective value (34.99), or check bulkDiscount(items) directly (0 today, 3 when fixed), so the expected failure is tied to the threshold bug.
